workClasses.direct: Work whose packet would cost as much as doing it: a question, an analysis, a config or doc edit, a change of a few lines the cooperator already knows exactly. Done inline with the project's checks; no agents.
workClasses.build: One verifiable block inside a clear write set for a light worker: a fix, a feature, a mechanical change of any size, reproducing a bug or tracing a cause. The cooperator briefs it with the goal, boundaries, sources, and check, without solving it first; the block is audited and reviewed before it is accepted.
workClasses.pipeline: Several blocks with disjoint write sets that need no decision from each other, run in parallel after open design decisions are made. Stage acceptance only when blocks interact in ways no block review saw.

orchestrator.role: brain: plan, brief, integrate, accept; writes code only in direct-class work

auditor.game: A lens runs only when the cooperator adds it for an uncovered area. It reports everything; the cooperator takes only real findings to the same worker. A lens with nothing real is retired for the block; one with real findings may check the fix.
auditor.coverage: A lens's round ends only when its auditor returns STATUS: complete (every assigned file read). An auditor that returns STATUS: partial or stops at its limit is continued on its NOT_REACHED files; nothing goes to the worker until every lens in the round is complete. At the token ceiling the lens moves to the next audit tier (workerBudgets.auditors).
auditor.budget: 40 tool calls per run, then STATUS: partial; separate from maxTurns 50.
auditor.mode: on-demand: only for an area the checks and the review do not cover

codexRunner.rule: Run every Codex call through the script with Bash run_in_background; never bare codex or codex exec. The script always exits: stdin from a file, approvals off, user config ignored, watchdog for silence, input requests, and total time. Read <name>.result.json; only status ok is a result.

hybrid.fallback: Codex unavailable or failing twice: auditor haiku xhigh and reviewers opus high through Agent; report the deviation once.

escalation.requires: State an unresolved reasoning problem and the expected benefit before using fable high. Existing high-effort roles fall back to opus high when fable is unavailable. Explicit user model, effort, and budget requirements remain binding; do not silently substitute for a strict requirement.

budgets.note: Defaults for role frontmatter and packets. maxTurns counts agent turns, not tool calls. User limits and project rules override them.

selectionRules.classifyFirst: Look only as far as the brief needs, then route: work whose packet would cost as much as doing it is the cooperator's (direct); any other verifiable block goes to a light worker (build), parts with disjoint write sets in parallel (pipeline).
selectionRules.reuse: Explicit task choice, active task context, or an applicable standing preference.
selectionRules.autonomous: Hybrid for described work, Enhanced for substantial unresolved design; proceed without asking. Applies to unattended runs.
selectionRules.askOnly: Long multi-stage work where the choice materially changes the approach and nothing applies.
selectionRules.runtimeMismatch: Model is set per Agent call; effort per role frontmatter or session. Report material deviations; explicit strict model, effort, and budget requirements remain binding.
selectionRules.hybrid: Default; Standard on the user's choice or when Codex is unavailable.

triggers: user asks for workforce, subagents, or multi-agent work
activation.otherwise: Normal single session; no agents spawned; the global block adds no other behavior.

haiku.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
haiku.tierNote: A request whose prompt (cache reads and writes included) is over 100k tokens pays the higher prices; keep a haiku worker's context below that.

modelResolution.note: Aliases are what the kit routes on; Claude Code and the provider decide the concrete model. A model release updates this record, not the workflow.

judging.real: In the diff or caused by it; breaks a quoted rule, document line, or acceptance line at a line that really violates it (the cooperator opens both); reproduces by a check or a concrete scenario.
judging.notReal: Theoretical risk, hypothetical input, work outside SCOPE, taste without a rule, duplicate of a rejected finding; anything the auditor filed under NOTES.
judging.who: The cooperator (orchestrator) judges; auditors and reviewers report everything.

continuity: Fixes go back to the same worker, the next audit round only to the auditors whose lens won the last round, the delta to the same reviewer, all through SendMessage (in Hybrid, the Codex thread is resumed). A fresh agent is for independence or a different model tier.

opus.then: the cooperator re-plans or asks the user

workerBudgets.rule: After the third attempt, or when the tool calls or tokens of the block are spent, unfinished work moves to the next tier of the profile's workerLadder as a fresh worker with the original packet, the cooperator's APPROACH, and the HANDOFF only. A submitted block at the limit is verified as it is; a later fix goes to the next tier. At the top of the ladder the cooperator re-plans or asks the user; explicit user limits are binding.
workerBudgets.auditors: An auditor on Codex Luna (haiku without Codex) whose count reaches 400k on a block hands its lens to Codex Sol xhigh (sonnet without Codex) in the auditor role on the same snapshot and round, with its NOT_REACHED files; its findings stay with the cooperator.
workerBudgets.accounting: An attempt is spent only by a run that ends without a result: the worker hit its BUDGET or turn limit, returned STATUS: handoff, or its fix left the finding open. A submitted block, or a fix that closes its finding, spends no attempt. Tool calls and tokens count for every run on the block, fixes included; a HANDOFF-only request is not a new run. Counters stay with the block when it is blocked, submitted, handed off, or put aside.
workerBudgets.usage: Claude Code's per-agent token count is the agent's context size at its last request, not its spend (2026-10-19: a sonnet worker reported 39,483 while processing about 346k); compare the agent's latest count with the ceiling and never add counts across its runs. Codex runs in Hybrid: compare tokens.threadTotal.uncached from the latest result.json. When a count is missing, go by attempts and tool calls and say so.
workerBudgets.enforcement: Instruction-level budgets; the runtime does not enforce them.

review.switch: policy.reviewBlock and policy.reviewStage, set at install (--set reviewBlock=off); every installed text renders from them.
review.delegatedBlocks: With reviewBlock on, a block a light worker submitted is accepted after an independent review by gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh; blocks ready together go to one review. With it off, the cooperator accepts on its own reading of the diff.
review.loop: Real findings go to the same worker; the same reviewer (or, with review off, the cooperator) checks the fixes and what they touch; the same finding twice without progress stops the loop for the cooperator's decision.
review.smallLocal: A small local change with a clear contract and passing checks may be accepted on the cooperator's own reading of the diff.
review.required: An independent review the project, the user, or the task requires runs whatever the switches say.
review.report: One line per reviewed block: REVIEW: rounds=<n> findings=<n> real=<n>.
